english.title: Cause use of snare / weapon to kill / take wild animal
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowingly caused the use of

(A)_[a self-locking snare]_
(B)_[a bow]_
(C)_[a crossbow ]_
(D)_[an explosive other than ammunition for a firearm, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_

for the purpose of killing or taking a wild animal
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(1)(d) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(ii) Section 21(6) provides arrangements for forfeiture
(iii) See Section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and Section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) See also offence wording H4659.
(v) See also failing to inspect, cause the inspection of or permit the inspection of snares on a daily basis at H4677, H4678 and H4679 respectively.
(vi) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation
